correctness.rationale: Strict radial kernel monotonicity is proved using a positive tridiagonal half-line evolution for ordinary heat differences and positive-stable subordination for all \(0<s<1\). The ℓ∞ norm of the gradient convolution is the coefficient ℓ¹ sum, which telescopes to twice the return probability, and one step signal attains it. For any \(0<a<b\le1\) the CDF difference of \(U^a,U^b\) changes sign exactly at spectral level one; the rescaled transform \(e^t(p_a-p_b)/t\) has a strictly negative derivative. Its positive t=0 value uses \(\mathbb E\log U=0\) and strictly convex spectral moments; its large-t limit is negative infinity. Hence one simple positive crossing, with rigorously oriented signs. The gamma and asymptotic constants follow from beta integration and low-frequency scaling. The current self-contained numerical checker ran successfully; finite samples are not used to prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The sharp ℓ∞-to-first-gradient smoothing norm is an operational stability constant for arbitrary bounded data and is attained by a single time- and order-independent signal. The all-pairs unique reversal is a structurally motivated obstruction to choosing one fractional diffusion order as uniformly best: every pair has exactly one crossover. The result adds global all-time exact constants and unique root structure to known fixed-order qualitative heat kernel bounds; it is not a fixed-size numerical table, routine substitution, or an isolated incremental estimate.
